name: Astera Labs
thesis: Astera Labs sells PCIe, CXL and Ethernet connectivity chips for AI racks; Q2 revenue was $392M (+105% y/y). It closed Oct 21 at $290.06, up 1.5% since Oct 16, after chips snapped an eight-day losing streak and Super Micro raised its forecast. Meta (Oct 21) narrowed 2026 capex to $135-145B and said it will keep 'investing aggressively' in 2027, which supports AI rack demand.
risks: A high multiple and a beta near 3.8 mean it swings 5%+ on sector headlines with no company news, and it still sits 24% below the Oct 7 close of $382.25.
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29; Q3 results Nov 3 after US close, call 4:30pm ET (08:30 AEDT Wed Nov 4).

name: Broadcom
thesis: Broadcom supplies custom AI accelerators (Google, Meta, OpenAI) plus Ethernet networking and VMware. It closed Oct 21 at $337.80, up 2.8% since Oct 16 as the chip selloff paused. Meta's Q3 capex of $34.9B (up from $31B in Q2) and a firmer 2026 range of $135-145B support custom-silicon volume.
risks: Broadcom is lining up financing for OpenAI's chip purchases, so worries about debt-funded AI build-outs hit it directly; Meta's Q3 free cash flow turned negative as capex outran operating cash.
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29; Q4 FY26 results around Dec 10 (not yet confirmed).

name: Celestica
thesis: Celestica builds 800G/1.6T networking switches, servers and storage for hyperscalers; it guided Q3 to $5.25-5.55B revenue and 2026 to $20.5B (+65%). It closed Oct 21 at $304.61, flat since Oct 16, while server peers Super Micro (+9.6%, raised forecast) and Dell (+5.3%) rallied. Q3 and an investor day with 2027 targets come next week.
risks: Single-digit hardware margins and a few hyperscaler customers; the investor day will be judged on 2027 targets against a possible capex digestion year.
catalyst: Q3 results Mon Oct 26 after US close (about 07:00 AEDT Tue Oct 27); call and Investor Day Tue Oct 27, 8:00am ET (23:00 AEDT Tue Oct 27).

name: Credo Technology
thesis: Credo sells active electrical cables, optical DSPs and retimers that connect GPUs and switches; fiscal Q1 2027 revenue was $479M (+115% y/y) at a 64.5% gross margin. It rose 6.28% on Oct 21 to $182.28 with networking names (Ciena +5.7%), ending a run of six straight declines and recovering 7.4% since Oct 16; no company news found.
risks: A handful of hyperscalers drive most revenue and growth is slowing (272% to 115% over four quarters), so one design loss or capex pause shows up within a quarter.
catalyst: Alphabet and Microsoft capex comments Oct 28-29; fiscal Q2 2027 results early December (date not announced).

name: SK hynix ADR
thesis: SK hynix is the leading HBM supplier to Nvidia and the number-two DRAM maker. The ADR closed Oct 21 at $143.25, up 5.0% since Oct 16 but still 27% below the Oct 2 close of $195.13. Lam's record quarter (Korea 20% of sales) and Meta's firmer capex range support memory demand; Q3 results on Oct 28 KST are the test.
risks: CXMT closing the density gap would pressure DRAM prices from 2027, and Q3 needs to show HBM pricing holding to justify buy/high after a 27% drawdown.
catalyst: Q3 results and call Wed Oct 28, 9:00am KST (11:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28), per Oct 14 Form 6-K; Samsung full Q3 results Oct 29.

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: Bloom makes solid-oxide fuel cells for onsite data-centre power; Q2 revenue was a record $1.07B and FY26 guidance is $3.9-4.2B, backed by Oracle (up to 2.8 GW) and Brookfield ($25B). It rose 7.24% on Oct 21 to $238.53 with AI-power names (Vertiv +4.3%, GE Vernova +4.0%) ahead of tonight's Q3 report; no company news found.
risks: Upside depends on Oracle and Brookfield deployments converting to revenue on time, and Q3 consensus EPS is a thin $0.14 for a stock that moves 6-10% on sector days.
catalyst: Q3 results Thu Oct 22 after US close, call 5:00pm ET (08:00 AEDT Fri Oct 23); Oracle Jupiter permit Nov 23.

name: GE Vernova
thesis: GE Vernova builds gas turbines, grid equipment and wind for the power build-out; Q2 orders rose 88% y/y and backlog is $176B. It rose 4.03% on Oct 21 to $925.92 after BofA previewed Q3 order growth of about 44% y/y (Buy, $1,310 target), and it won a 9E turbine for a 372 MW plant in Cote d'Ivoire.
risks: Q2 EPS missed ($2.47 vs $3.17) and wind still loses money, so another margin miss on Oct 28 would test the premium multiple; the stock is below its 50- and 200-day averages.
catalyst: Q3 results Wed Oct 28, webcast 7:30am ET (22:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: Vertiv
thesis: Vertiv sells power, thermal and liquid-cooling gear for data centres; it guided Q3 sales to $3.65-3.85B and lifted FY26 EPS to $6.65-6.75. It rose 4.26% on Oct 21 to $212.15, ending a losing run, as AI-infrastructure names rallied; no company news found.
risks: The stock trades on the 2027 hyperscaler-capex debate rather than guidance, and price competition in liquid cooling is rising.
catalyst: Q3 results Wed Oct 28 before US open; call 11:00am ET (02:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29).

name: Robinhood
thesis: Robinhood is a retail brokerage adding prediction markets, perpetual futures and Robinhood Agents; Q2 revenue was $1.31B (+32%). Preliminary September data to Sep 24 showed about $267B equity volume, 234M options contracts and 4.4B event contracts; full September data comes with Q3. It closed Oct 21 at $101.93, up 3.1% since Oct 16.
risks: Revenue tracks crypto and equity volumes, and crypto notional of about $17B in September (to Sep 24) is soft, so Q3 depends on options and event contracts.
catalyst: Q3 results and full September operating data Tue Oct 27 after close, video call 5pm ET (08:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: MercadoLibre runs Latin America's largest marketplace, logistics network and Mercado Pago; Q2 net revenue was $10.2B (+50% y/y) while operating income fell 17%. It closed Oct 21 at $1,854.88, up 1.1% since Oct 16. Brazil's runoff has tightened: Quaest (Oct 21) has Flavio Bolsonaro 45%, Lula 44%, down from a 2-point lead, within a 2-point margin.
risks: The Oct 25 runoff is now a statistical tie and a Lula win would unwind part of the election premium; margins are being absorbed by the credit book and logistics.
catalyst: Brazil runoff Sun Oct 25 (results Mon Oct 26 morning AEDT); Q3 results Nov 4 (provisional).

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Cloudflare runs a global edge network selling security, CDN, zero-trust and the Workers developer platform; Q2 revenue was $696M (+36%) and it guided Q3 to $736-737M. It rose 5.32% on Oct 21 to $307.22 as security stocks rallied on a critical PHP flaw. Q3 is confirmed for Nov 5, a week later than estimated.
risks: The stock has had 38 moves of more than 5% in a year and is only 11% below the consensus target, so Q3 has to beat and raise.
catalyst: Q3 results Thu Nov 5 after US close, call 5:00pm ET (09:00 AEDT Fri Nov 6), per company notice of Oct 13.

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Sea runs Shopee, Monee (digital finance) and Garena across Southeast Asia and Brazil; Q2 revenue was $7.79B (+48%). On Oct 20 a CEO memo said Sea will sell AI cloud services to enterprises (Sea Cloud, against AWS and Alibaba Cloud) and is weighing an IPO of Monee. The stock fell 16.9% in three sessions to $77.94 on Oct 21, near its 52-week low of $77.05. Downgraded to watch/low until Q3 shows whether cloud spending eats Shopee's margin gains.
risks: A new cloud business adds spending with no disclosed budget while Shopee is already fighting TikTok Shop, Temu and Shein; DBS cut to Hold ($105) on 2027 margin worries.
catalyst: Q3 results ~Nov 10 (TBC); any detail on Sea Cloud capex or Monee IPO timing.

name: Keyence
thesis: Keyence sells machine-vision, sensors and measurement gear direct to factories with industry-leading margins and no debt. It closed Oct 21 at JPY 80,860 (about US$512 at 157.88), flat since Oct 16, steady through the US chip selloff. Lam's record quarter and guide above consensus point to continued fab spending, a core end market.
risks: Orders follow the factory-capex cycle within a quarter, Q1 EPS slightly missed, and a stronger yen cuts reported overseas revenue.
catalyst: Fiscal Q2 results Thu Oct 29 (per StockAnalysis); BOJ decision Oct 30.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: ASML is the only supplier of EUV lithography tools; Q3 sales were a record EUR 11.66B and it guided 2026 to EUR 44-45B, saying 2027-28 supply will not fully meet demand. Lam (Oct 21) beat with record revenue of $8.22B (+22% q/q) and guided Dec quarter to $8.60B, above consensus, confirming strong fab spending. The ADR closed Oct 21 at $1,676.69, up 2.1% since Oct 16.
risks: Lam fell about 6% after hours despite the beat, a sign semicap is priced for perfection; China is about 20% of ASML sales and export rules can change.
catalyst: Interim dividend EUR 1.88 payable Nov 4; Q4 results January (date TBC).

name: Teradyne
thesis: Teradyne makes test equipment for AI accelerators, HBM and mobile chips, plus Universal Robots; Q3 guidance is $1.20-1.30B revenue. It rebounded 6.3% since Oct 16 to $345.49 on Oct 21 as memory and chip-test names recovered (Advantest +5.3% in Tokyo). Lam's beat and Korea at 20% of its sales support memory test demand; Q3 date is now confirmed.
risks: HBM test is a large part of the story, so a weak SK hynix or Samsung print the same week would hit it; test spend is lumpy and concentrated in a few customers.
catalyst: Q3 results Tue Oct 27 at 4:30pm ET or later (07:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28); call Wed Oct 28, 8:30am ET (23:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).
